div.head: V Atr 9.1
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe þæs geswican wille ⁊ clænnesse healdan, hæbbe he Godes miltse, ⁊ þær to eacan to woroldweorðscype, þæt he sy þegenweres ⁊ þegenrihtes wyrðe, ge on life ge on legere.
⁊ se ðe þæs geswican wille ⁊ clænnesse healdan, hæbbe he Godes miltse, ⁊ þær to eacan to woroldweorðscype, þæt he sy þegenweres ⁊ þegenrihtes wyrðe, ge on life ge on legere.
⁊ se þe þæs geswican wille ⁊ clænnesse healdan, habbe he Godes mildse, ⁊ þar to eacan to worldwurðscipe þæt he sy þegenweres ⁊ þegenrihtes wurðe, ge on life ge on legere.

But he who will turn from marriage and observe celibacy shall obtain the favour of God, and in addition, as worldly honour, he shall enjoy the wergeld and the privileges of a thegn, both during his life and after his death.
Und wer hiervon abstehen und Keuschheit bewahren will, erhalte er Gottes Gnade und ausserdem als weltlichen Ehrenrang, dass er Thegn-Wergeldes und Thegn-Vorrechts geniesse, wie im Leben so im Grabe.

And whoever will desist from this and keep chastity, let him have God's mercy and, in addition, as a worldly honour, that he be entitled to a thegn's wergild and a thegn's rights, both in life and in the grave.
